evidence:
MATH — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, NOT TRUSTED. I re-implemented xpAt() from the reference prose in my own script and diffed all 121 entries against src/js/engine/xp.js: 0 differences. All 22 published cumulative thresholds and all 22 per-level deltas reproduce exactly (L50=101,333 / L92=6,517,253 / L99=13,034,431 / L120=104,273,167), plus the 8 intermediate pacing checkpoints (L25=7,842 ... L95=8,771,558). Doubling ratio 1.9946 @L10 -> 1.999701 @L66 -> 1.999969 @L92. The 1->92 == 92->99 identity is approximate in reality (6,517,253 vs 6,517,178, delta -75, 1.2e-5 relative) and they assert it with a 0.001 tolerance — correct, not fudged. XP table entries are all integers and max value is well inside 2^53 despite the Float64Array backing.

SELFTEST IS NOT RIGGED. Critical check: I edited one digit in reference/melvor-math.md (13,034,431 -> 13,034,999) and re-ran. Result: '123 passed, 1 failed'. The tables are genuinely parsed out of the markdown at test time, so the assertions are coupled to the document, not to a transcribed fixture.

DETERMINISM — VERIFIED IN MY OWN HARNESS, outside their test runner. 2h streams under seed 0xC0FFEE hashed to dc1dbd88b4cf1a75 across two runs: byte-identical. Fast event-jump advance() produced the identical hash to naive tick-by-tick. Uneven 377-tick chunking reached the identical final state (the one diff my first pass flagged was my own test's timestamp argument, not engine state).

OFFLINE REPLAY — 24h naive live ticking (1,728,000 ticks) equals offlineReplay(24h) exactly; equals 24 separate 1h advances exactly; equals serialise-at-tick-12345-then-resume exactly. Three days away replays exactly 24h. Perf: 1.728M ticks in 26ms (~68,000 ticks/ms) — the 'under a second on a phone' requirement is met with ~40x headroom.

EDGE CASES I PROBED THAT THEIR SUITE DOES NOT. Artisan running out of inputs mid-replay stops with reason 'out-of-materials' at tick 360, and fast==naive across that discontinuity. Offline combat death: deaths=1, reason 'death', and fast==naive across the death too. Clock moved backwards (device time change) yields 0 ticks, not a negative or absurd replay. Zero elapsed yields 0. levelAt(-5) and levelAt(NaN) both clamp to 1. Nothing broke.

CONTENT — CLEAN. My own grep (not their scanner) across src/data/ for the RuneScape metal ladder, RS skill names, RS item/place names, and ~60 FFVI proper nouns returned zero hits in shipped strings; the only matches were code comments citing the reference doc and generic stat words (hp/attack). DB validates at boot and refuses to load on a dangling item id or an unobtainable item.

ECONOMY IS ACTUALLY DESIGNED. Three gather skills port the reference's woodcutting/mining/fishing curves exactly (Boughcraft XP 10/15/22/30/40/60/80/100/180 at 3/4/5/6/8/10/12/20/15s — the published table, renamed), which is what 'take the MATH, never the content' asked for. The invented layers are real design: Sigilwork values climb a clean ~3.7x/step geometric ladder; every skill carries exactly one deliberate value inversion that is never the top rung (Sunwood at 400 Cogs is rung 8 of 9), preserving the reference's 'make the player choose XP or GP' read. Kilnwork has genuine multi-input depth (Ninefold Ingot consumes aetherite-core x2 + warden-alloy + ember-void x3). Faucet spans 2,384 -> 11.81B Cogs/hr (1.5e7). Best non-combat loop (Sigilwork) is throttled to 3.4% by Aether Shard income, which only drops from tier-5+ combat — so the two halves of the endgame are deliberately interlocked rather than independent, and combat/craft lands at 99.09x.

I TRIED TO BREAK THE SINKS AND FAILED. My hypothesis was the classic idle failure: sinks priced for mid-game while the endgame faucet outruns them. Measured: clasps 93.71M + waystations 862M + tools 5.4M + relics 9.43B + ascension rites 64.4B = ~75B of sink against 14.99B/hr endgame income, i.e. ~5 hours. The terminal sinks genuinely scale with the terminal faucet. Hypothesis wrong; economy is sunk end to end.

WHERE IT IS WEAK (all in the report page, none in the numbers). (1) Structure: section 1 is 27% of the document and 124 flat pass-rows precede the first chart at ~23,000px. Section 6 is another 26.7%. (2) The .formula blocks are overflow-x:auto with white-space:pre but get NO swipe hint and NO fade gradient — unlike .tablewrap, which gets both — so on 390px the MXP formula clips mid-token at '(UnlockedActions * TotalMasteryInSkill / (RecipeCo' with nothing signalling it scrolls. That is the single most important line in section 3, hidden. Screenshot: progress/shots/engine-economy-r1-formula-clip.png. (3) The XP chart's '92 — halfway' and '99' annotations visually collide. (4) The wide tables push XP/s and Cogs/hr off-viewport behind 'swipe for the rest of the row'.

CHARTS DO EXIST (I initially miscounted from a slice): four real SVGs — the log-scaled XP curve with 50/92/99/120 markers, the throughput-vs-reduction hyperbola, a 658px log-scaled faucet bar ladder colour-split gold=craft / violet=combat, and the clasp cost curve. The faucet ladder does answer the brief's 'hour one vs endgame at a glance'.
blindResult: Not a like-for-like comparison, and I want to be honest about that rather than score it as a win it did not earn. reference/shots/ui-bar.png is a game HOME screen — hero art, giant serif 128, beveled gold CLAIM, currency pills, bottom nav. balance.html is an internal engineering/design report. Stripped of labels, anyone would pick ui-bar.png as 'the shipped commercial product' because it is a product surface and this is a document. What the blind test DOES show is that they read as the same product's design system: identical dark-navy ground, the same gold-and-violet-only accent discipline, the same serif display face, 16px rounded panels with hairline borders. Against the bar that actually judges this piece — reference/melvor-math.md — it does not merely tie, it reproduces every published table exactly and then builds an original priced economy on top. That is the comparison that counts here, and it wins it.
